title: Passenger class pivot per airline
statementMd:
For each airline show the number of bookings by `economy`, `business` and `first` as three columns.

Expected columns: `name`, `economy`, `business`, `first`.

Tables: `airlines`, `airports`, `flights`, `bookings`.

Row order does not matter.
solutionMd:
```sql
SELECT a.name, SUM(b.seat_class = 'economy') AS economy, SUM(b.seat_class = 'business') AS business, SUM(b.seat_class = 'first') AS first FROM bookings b JOIN flights f ON f.id = b.flight_id JOIN airlines a ON a.code = f.airline_code GROUP BY a.code, a.name;
```

Compare with your own query; the result sets must match.
